newsitem.title: USA: Bill passed on U.S. government electronic data.
newsitem.headline: Bill passed on U.S. government electronic data.

text.p: A bill to make electronically stored federal information available to the public was appproved by the House Tuesday.

The bill, passed 402-0, would extend the Freedom of Information Act to include electronic information. The Senate was also expected to pass the legislation soon and send it to President Clinton for his signature.
The act, which now applies to printed information, allows members of the public to obtain copies of government documents unless the information cannot be released for national security reasons.
"This will bring the FOIA from the technological stone age into the information age," said Representative Carolym Maloney, a New York Democrat who is one of the bill's sponsors.

"Electronic access is a logical extension of the freedom of information law. More and more today, to be well-informed, you have to have computer access to information," added Sen. Patrick Leahy, a Vermont Democrat.

Maloney said because of complaints about delays in providing information, federal agencies will also be required to report on the number of FOIA requests they receive each year and how long it takes them to process the requests.
"By the time many FOIA information requests are fulfilled, the information is often useless to the requestor, if the requestor hasn't died of old age," she said.
